        Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur confirmed Monday that running back Josh Jacobs is not expected to play in a crucial Thanksgiving Eve game against the Los Angeles Rams because of a finger injury he sustained in Week 9.Jacobs suffered the injury early in the Packers' beatdown of the New England Patriots and had surgery shortly thereafter. He had tried to re-enter the game but had trouble gripping the football.Running the ball has been a historic weakness for the Packers this year. Green Bay's 3.1 yards per carry is last in the NFL and on pace to be the worst by any team since the 2000 Chargers. The Packers are getting only 20% of their offensive yards on the ground, which is on pace to be the worst single-season mark since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger.Jacobs missed the first six weeks of the season while on the commissioner exempt list after being charged with two misdemeanors stemming from a May arrest. He scored three touchdowns in three games, but his 2.2 yards per carry is actually the worst of Green Bay's running backs. It's been a mess all year, both in runners and blockers.

The Rams' defense ranks 10th in yards per carry allowed overall but is first since Week 8, allowing just 2.9 yards per carry. As such, Jordan Love and wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden figure to carry a heavy burden.Kaleb Johnson, who played well in Jacobs' place after he left the Patriots game, could project to see the most early-down touches, though the rotation is convoluted. MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks may see more passing-down work.
This game is absolutely critical for both teams, as the Packers and the Rams are both 6-4. According to CBS Sports forecasting and projections, the Packers currently have a 38% chance to make the playoffs, while the Rams are right behind them at 35%. Green Bay's postseason chances would jump to 60% with a win; Los Angeles' would improve to 48% with a victory.

title: UCLA optimistic Ty Dieffenbach could return from lower body injury as Bruins face potential CFP run - CBS Sports
description: Good news could be on the horizon for UCLA in the Big Ten title and CFP picture

Good news could be on the horizon for UCLA in the Big Ten title and CFP picture
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Nov 23, 2026

    11:25 am ET

            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        UCLA starting quarterback Ty Dieffenbach's injury may not be as serious as initially feared coming out of Saturday's overtime loss at Michigan. There's "optimism" after further testing over the weekend that Dieffenbach will return at some point this season, according to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz.Dieffenbach was carted off with a hip injury after landing awkwardly in the first overtime after Michigan linebacker Troy Bowles brought him to the ground. All of Bowles' weight came down on Dieffenbach, who was on the turf several minutes before going to a local hospital for evaluation.UCLA coach Bob Chesney said after the game he wasn't sure of the severity. CBS Los Angeles' Jill Painter Lopez later reported Dieffenbach's X-rays had come back negative."I don't know. I have no clue. No clue till we see him; I haven't seen him. Just walked off the field, came into here," Chesney said of Dieffenbach's status. "It's tough to lose anybody. When Aiden (Mizell) went down, that wasn't easy. Those things are tough, but it's the game that we play."Bruins third-team quarterback Madden Iamaleava came in for Dieffenbach and didn't have success, going 0-for-1 passing,  rushing twice for no yards and having an unsuccessful two-point conversion try in overtime.
"We trust Madden. We just got to be able to deliver in those moments," Chesney said. "It was hard to run the ball a little bit, and I think we had a couple opportunities in the pass game."UCLA's CFP, Big Ten Championship statusComing off their first loss of the campaign, the Bruins are sure to fall from their current No. 4 spot in Tuesday night's fourth playoff rankings. UCLA dropped six spots to No. 10 in Sunday's latest AP Poll, suggesting a significant downgrade with Dieffenbach's status up in the air.UCLA is currently a 6.5-point underdog in Saturday's regular-season finale against USC at the Rose Bowl. A win for the Bruins puts them in next weekend's Big Ten Championship Game, the last of its kind with college football moving to a 24-team playoff next fall.
UCLA can also get there with a loss for Oregon against Washington. With Dieffenbach's availability unknown for the weekend, CBS Sports' current end-of-season playoff projection has the Bruins on the outside looking in as the Big Ten's third-place finisher after a loss to the Trojans this weekend.

title: Steelers' DK Metcalf denies trying to poke Eagles' Cooper DeJean in the eye - CBS Sports
description: Metcalf was ejected from the game and will likely face further discipline from the NFL
body:
Metcalf was ejected from the game and will likely face further discipline from the NFL
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:11 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        DK Metcalf says that he wasn't intentionally trying to poke Cooper DeJean in the eye during an altercation that took place between the two during Sunday's game between the Steelers and Eagles. Metcalf's encounter with DeJean led to his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty of the third quarter, which ultimately resulted in his ejection. Metcalf will surely be fined by the NFL and could possibly face a suspension as a repeat offender. "I just wish I would have been there for my team," Metcalf said on Monday when asked about the incident. When asked about his struggles to keep his composure on the field at times, Metcalf said, "I think you got to ask the people that seem to do that to me." 
Metcalf then corrected a reporter who alluded to his attempt to poke DeJean in the eye. "I didn't try to poke him in the eye," Metcalf said. Regardless, cameras did capture Metcalf poking his finger inside DeJean's facemask before the two were separated. 
When asked about the incident on Sunday, DeJean said that Metcalf "almost" hit him in the eye but didn't. 
"You know, things like that happen in football," he said. "It wasn't anything crazy; no one was really saying anything. It was just, you know, two guys going at it. He was trying to block me. I was trying to get him off of me. Things like that, and that obviously carried over to whatever that was at the end, or when he got thrown out." DeJean said that Metcalf's frustration may have stemmed from the fact that he had not had much impact on the game. Metcalf had just one catch for two yards prior to being ejected. He has six catches for 118 yards and one touchdown combined across Pittsburgh's last four games. His 3.6 receptions per game, 43.4 yards per game, and 5.9 yards per target would all either tie or set new career lows if the season ended today. Metcalf, however, does not attribute what happened Sunday to his lack of production. 
"No, I mean we're winning," he said, before correcting himself. "We were winning." Metcalf said he doesn't know whether he will face further discipline from either the Steelers or the NFL. "You gotta ask Omar (Khan) that, or anybody else other than DK," he said. Metcalf, who served a two-game suspension last season after getting into an altercation with a Lions fan, was fined nearly $12,000 earlier this season for an unnecessary roughness penalty that was assessed during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss to Cleveland. 
Metcalf has been fined over $750,000 by the NFL over his career between the suspension, multiple unsportsmanlike conduct penalties and other infractions, according to Spotrac. That number will surely rise in the coming days. And, as noted above, Metcalf could also be suspended for Pittsburgh's Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos.

        For the first time this season, there is a new No. 1 team in the AP Top 25 poll. Houston jumped seven spots to No. 1 in the updated rankings released Monday after a flawless week at the Players Era 8 in Las Vegas that included a win over the previous No. 1 team, Florida. With Houston jumping to No. 1, it's the first time the Cougars have occupied that spot since the first in-season poll last season. The Cougars began the 2025-26 campaign ranked No. 2 behind Purdue before jumping the Boilermakers for the top spot. Houston's jump of seven spots from last week's ranking of No. 8 tied for the biggest jump for a No. 1 team from the previous week in AP poll history (since 1948-49). With four of the top five teams (Florida, Michigan State, UConn and Duke) losing last week, there was bound to be significant movement throughout the poll. The team that took the biggest hit in this week's poll was Duke. The Blue Devils dropped 11 spots to No. 16 after losing at home to Illinois in blowout fashion. 
Duke has a massive showdown on Wednesday in Las Vegas against No. 10 UConn, which suffered its first loss of the season on the road against No. 8 Arizona. The Blue Devils also face No. 3 Florida next month in the ACC/SEC Challenge. Indiana entered the rankings for the first time this season and checked in at No. 23 in the poll after a 2-0 week that included wins over Arkansas at Madison Square Garden and Kentucky at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. Indiana is off to a 6-0 start for the second consecutive season under coach Darian DeVries.

With Indiana entering for the first time, that meant at least one team had to drop out entirely. Reigning national champion Michigan dropped out of the poll after suffering a loss against Villanova on the road. The loss dropped the Wolverines to 3-2, which matched the number of losses they had in the regular season during their title season.
Duke plummets out of the top 10One of the biggest surprises of the poll this week was the fact that Duke fell only 11 spots to No. 16 after losing to Illinois at home. On paper, Duke has losses against two top 15 teams (Illinois and Michigan State), but the problem is that the Blue Devils haven't looked competitive in either game. I projected the Blue Devils to fall in the 20s, but the voters put them at 16. Duke will have a chance to prove why it should be ranked as a top 20 team against UConn on Wednesday in Las Vegas. If Duke loses that game, it will likely drop out of next week's poll.Welcome to the party, MemphisFor the first time this season, Memphis is ranked. It came about a week too late because the Tigers should've been ranked last week. Memphis has a very solid resume with wins over Louisville, VCU and Iowa State through the first three weeks of the season. Penny Hardaway deserves a ton of credit for getting his team off to a hot start.Reigning champ Michigan drops out entirely It was not a good week for the state of Michigan in college basketball. Michigan dropped out of the poll completely after losing to Villanova on the road, which marked its second loss in five games. Meanwhile, Michigan State wasn't much better. The Spartans made just nine field goals during a loss to Tennessee on the road and had the second-biggest drop (nine spots) in the poll behind Duke.

title: Serie A hot takes: Christian Pulisic finally at his best; Inter won't be winning the Scudetto - CBS Sports
description: Elsewhere, Genoa will end up in the top 10, and we saw that coming
body:
Elsewhere, Genoa will end up in the top 10, and we saw that coming

        Serie A was back over the weekend in the first matchday after the international break and there were plenty of interesting things to look at. First of all, Atalanta and Inter showcased a spectacular 4-4 draw in Bergamo, which underlined once again the defensive issues of the team led by Cristian Chivu. Elsewhere, AS Roma, Napoli, Juventus and AC Milan all won and had some convincing performances. Now, it's time for our Serie A hot takes.  Don't miss all the Serie A action all season long across Paramount+, CBS Sports Network and CBS Sports Golazo Network. From Italy's biggest teams to America's biggest stars, Serie A has it all, and Paramount+ is the home for every minute of the action until a Scudetto winner is crowned.    Inter can't win the title again Inter are in trouble, once again, for the same issues. The team led by Chivu managed to draw a game against Atalanta where they scored four goals and Inter striker Francesco Pio Esposito netted a hat-trick. This is worrying, especially considering the defensive record of the Nerazzurri, who have conceded 17 goals in 12 games so far, and are the ninth-best Serie A team if we look at the goals conceded, showing a disappointing defending record which makes things really hard for Inter in the long term. Despite having some of the best defenders in the league, Inter have been surprisingly vulnerable defensively since the start of the season. They've shown far too many weaknesses to be considered serious contenders for the Serie A title. You simply cannot win the Scudetto if you continue defending like this. 
 Pulisic is on fire (finally!) Christian Pulisic has finally landed. After a slow start to the season due to the injury that affected him at the end of the 2026 World Cup, the American striker is now in his best condition under Ruben Amorim. Pulisic has scored four goals in the last five Serie A games, and looks to be finally at his best. The American striker has just extended his deal until 2031 and he's one of the most crucial players for the Italian club. Things are finally looking great for him and AC Milan, but they need to keep going like this.  
 Genoa to end up in the top 10 We probably forgot about Genoa a little too soon. The team led by Daniele De Rossi had a slow start to the season but they are now in great form with four wins in the last five Serie A games and are in the top 10 of the standings. Before the start of the new campaign, I thought they could be the surprise package of the season. So far, I've been proven wrong, but they could still be getting back into contention for a place in the race. Their striker, Milutin Osmajić, has been phenomenal, scoring six goals in the opening 11 games of his Serie A season. Not bad at all.

title: Why Mets owner Steve Cohen was willing to give Tarik Skubal the most lucrative pitcher contract in MLB history - CBS Sports
description: Cohen said he doesn't 'have to worry' about his new $450 million ace 'pitching in New York'
body:
Cohen said he doesn't 'have to worry' about his new $450 million ace 'pitching in New York'
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:06 am ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The New York Mets have landed two-time Cy Young-winning lefty Tarik Skubal, the offseason's top free agent, with a record-shattering nine-year contract worth $450 million. It far exceeds Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million deal with the Los Angeles Dodgers, which was the previous record guarantee for a pitcher. Every contract that long and that pricey carries risk and surely makes even the league's wealthiest owner a wee bit queasy. After meeting with Skubal in California last week, though, Mets owner Steve Cohen came away convinced Skubal was his guy and that he would have no issues settling into his new environment."He's going to be great for the clubhouse ... I don't have to worry about him pitching in New York," Cohen told the New York Post on Sunday, before the deal went official. "... He's an outstanding individual. He's bright. He's a student of the game. He's very impressive."
        
            
                Why a long-term mega deal for Tarik Skubal isn't actually all that risky
                
                    Matt Snyder                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The "can he handle New York?" thing tends to get overblown, but it is a real consideration. It's a different market with different demands and you never truly know how a player will handle it until he experiences it. I think Skubal will be more than fine in New York because I don't think you can be as successful as he's been without embracing the spotlight, but I don't know that for certain. No one does.
Skubal has proven his bona fides on the biggest stages. He's been sensational in eight career postseason starts, pitching to a 2.13 ERA with 70 strikeouts in 50 ⅔ innings. All indications are that Skubal is a good teammate who fit in well with the Dodgers following his midseason trade from the Detroit Tigers.Now 30, Skubal posted a 2.72 ERA in 158 ⅔ innings around his NanoScope elbow procedure this past season. He leads all pitchers with 18.0 WAR over the last three years despite missing time with injury this year.
The Mets went 74-88 and finished in last place in 2026. They were baseball's most disappointing team and signing Skubal is an enormous step toward making sure it doesn't happen again.

A five-game SEC winning streak pushes Steve Sarkisian's squad to No. 4 as the nation's top two-loss team

        With just one week left in the college football regular season, the rankings are starting to settle into what will be their final form to tell the story of 2026. Quality is being tested under the toughest conditions in conference play, with adversity that includes injuries at key positions and tough breaks in close games. Teams that can survive those tests continue to win and move up in the rankings, while others break under pressure and suffer the rankings drop that follows a late-season loss. Texas has proven it is better than its midseason form, continuing to stack wins after a 4-2 start. The Longhorns have won five games in a row against SEC competition, and after beating Arkansas by 42 points in the home finale, are moving up in the CBS Sports 138. Our voters, which include experts from CBS Sports and 247Sports, have bumped Texas up four spots from No. 8 to No. 4, making Steve Sarkisian's crew the highest-ranked two-loss team in the country, Tennessee is another team that continues to show some strong late-season form, staying in the hunt for the SEC Championship Game with a 27-13 win against LSU in Knoxville. The Vols bumped up three spots in our rankings, now checking in at No. 7 just ahead of one-loss Wake Forest and one-loss Texas Tech. Part of the reason for the shakeup in the top 10 is the one-two punch of UCLA and Indiana taking losses in Week 12. The Bruins dropped six spots from No. 4 to No. 10 after taking their first loss of the season, while the Hoosiers had a similar rankings result (down to No. 12 from No. 6) after dropping to 9-2 with an overtime loss at Washington. While those results were bad for the Big Ten's representation at the top of the rankings, they provided good news for teams like Oregon and Iowa that are now firmly in the Big Ten championship and College Football Playoff picture heading into rivalry weekend. 
Those shake-ups inside the top 15 are far from the only notable changes in the CBS Sports 138 this week, so we've highlighted several more below. You can see those adjustments, with commentary, in the Mover's Report below the top 25 table. College football experts from CBS Sports and 247Sports contribute ballots each week, which are averaged together for our rankings. You can see the top 25 below and 26-138 on our rankings page.
RankTeamRecordPrevious1Georgia10-112Utah11-023Notre Dame10-134Texas9-285Miami10-156Alabama9-277Tennessee9-2108Wake Forest10-199Texas Tech10-11210UCLA10-1411BYU9-21112Indiana9-2613Iowa9-21314Oregon8-31415USC8-31816Arizona8-31917Houston8-32018Louisville8-32319Ohio State7-41520Oklahoma7-43021Liberty10-13422Missouri7-43323Boise State9-21724Nebraska7-43225Florida7-428Biggest movers No. 21 Liberty (+13): The high win count was going to end up providing plenty of opportunity to move up as other teams take losses, and now that Liberty is 10-1 and riding a 10-game winning streak, there was a move into the top 25. The Flames have been getting some top 20 consideration elsewhere, but the strength of schedule has limited the ability to crash the rankings. Now, the weight of the wins is too much to overlook when picking teams in this range of a ballot. No. 49 Michigan (+13): One of the biggest wins of the weekend deserves one of the most notable moves in the rankings, and while Michigan's 6-5 record is far less impressive than preseason expectations, the Wolverines do have an extremely impressive resume among other 6-5 teams. Wins against UCLA and Oklahoma are hard to match in this range, which made it easy to give some credit after handing the Bruins their first loss of the season. No. 22 Missouri (+11): It turns out not having to play the Georgia defense or the Texas defense has really opened things up for Austin Simmons and Missouri. The Tigers bounced back from a disappointing start to November with a 28-14 win against Kentucky that really bolstered the team's rankings profile. It's the first win for Missouri against a team with a current winning record since Florida on Oct. 3, and provides some momentum heading into an intriguing regular season finale against Oklahoma on Saturday. No. 20 Oklahoma (+10): Speaking of the Sooners, Brent Venables has Oklahoma riding high with three straight wins and two of them have come against other quality competition in the SEC. Beating a seven-loss Texas A&M team didn't spark this move as much as the continued recent success, since Oklahoma now has multiple wins against top-30 teams (Texas, Florida, Ole Miss) in SEC play. No. 41 Northwestern (-10): Things have continued to unravel after an impressive start to the season for Northwestern, as injuries have mounted and offensive production has waned. The quality of competition has ramped up, and the winning has slowed down, revealing a less impressive engine under the hood of the expensive sports car of a roster in Baton Rouge. No. 28 Kentucky (-12): Like LSU, Kentucky just took its third loss in a row and now is being held up by the strength of some of its better wins from earlier in the season. body:
The tournament returns to North America after Canada hosted in 2015, while the U.S. resumes hosting duties for the Women's World Cup for the first time since 2003
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 23, 2026

    10:17 am ET

        FIFA confirmed its plans to stage the 2031 Women's World Cup in North America, with the joint bid from the U.S., Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica officially getting the green light at an extraordinary FIFA Congress in Zurich on Monday.The announcement comes a year after the co-hosts formalized their commitment to put in a bid, one that was ultimately the only contender for the 2031 tournament. FIFA also confirmed its decision to host the 2035 Women's World Cup in the U.K.; that bid was also unopposed heading into Monday's meeting.The Women's World Cup will return to North America for the first time since Canada hosted the tournament in 2015, while the U.S. will host the competition for the first time since 2003. Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica are all first-time hosts of the women's tournament, their inclusion in the bid part of an effort to accelerate the growth of women's soccer across the region. The 2031 World Cup, though, will also be another opportunity to showcase the growth of the women's game -- the U.S. has long been a hotbed for the sport, but its embrace of women's soccer has only grown since 2003, particularly with the increasing popularity of the uber-successful U.S. women's national team and the professionalization of the NWSL.FIFA will return to the U.S. and Mexico fairly quickly after the two countries, alongside Canada, hosted the men's World Cup earlier this year, an experience that will prove to be relevant to the 2031 organizers from a logistical standpoint. Just as the men's World Cup did in 2026, the women's tournament will expand to 48 teams in 2031, a choice that ultimately resulted in the creation of a new competition footprint. U.S. Soccer president Cindy Parlow Cone said last year that the expansion was the main impetus for including Costa Rica and Jamaica in a bid that was once envisioned as a 32-team competition in just the U.S. and Mexico.
"As soon as I knew for sure that was in the works, I went to [Concacaf] president Victor Montagliani and talked to him about our vision and that we wanted to make it bigger and include more countries throughout Concacaf and wanted to work with him to pick which countries would be best suited," Parlow Cone said at the time. "Obviously, quality of teams, stadiums, infrastructure. Outside of stadiums, like hotels, training facilities also went into the decision."Monday's announcement officially kicks off the process for a tournament FIFA hopes will attract more than 4.5 million spectators and estimates will generate more than $4 billion in revenue, which would make it the highest revenue-generating women's sporting event in history.The host-city race beginsFIFA's bid evaluation report lists 20 stadiums that could host games, though the actual bid includes more than 30 cities and 45 venues that will vie for the chance to host games in 2031. Most of the 14 cities across the U.S. and Mexico that hosted the 2026 tournament are back in the mix, including the host of this year's final, MetLife Stadium in the New York area, and the semifinal venues of AT&T Stadium in the Dallas suburbs and Atlanta's Mercedes-Benz Stadium. A few cities that did not make the cut last time around, though, are also interested -- Denver's Empower Field is on the list, as is the under-construction stadium in Washington, D.C., that the NFL's Washington Commanders will call home and is expected to be complete in 2030.
The list of contenders in Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica is understandably smaller considering each country's size and the resources available. While competition to host games could heat up around North America, a fairly straightforward answer is expected in Jamaica. The under-renovation Independence Park in the capital city of Kingston is the only venue listed in the bid.Host cities listed in the 2031 bidUnited StatesArrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Mo.AT&T Stadium in Arlington, TexasBank of America Stadium in Charlotte, N.C.Camping World Stadium in Orlando, Fla.Empower Field at Mile High in DenverGeodis Park in Nashville, Tenn.Lumen Field in SeattleMercedes-Benz Stadium in AtlantaMetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, N.J.New Stadium at RFK Campus in Washington, D.C.NRG Stadium in HoustonSoFi Stadium in Inglewood, Calif.Snapdragon Stadium in San DiegoU.S. Bank Stadium in MinneapolisMexicoEstadio Akron in Zapopan, MexicoEstadio Azteca in Mexico CityEstadio BBVA in Guadalupe, MexicoEstadio Corona in Torreon, MexicoCosta RicaCosta Rica National Stadium in San Jose, Costa RicaJamaicaIndependence Park in Kingston, JamaicaA new tournament format in the mixThe 2031 bid is attracting more interest from potential host cities than the 2026 tournament did for one reason in particular -- tournament organizers are inviting bids from a wider range of stadiums this time around.This year's men's World Cup was hosted exclusively in NFL stadiums or similarly sized venues in Canada and Mexico, some of which will likely stage games again in 2031 and welcome the teams that are expected to draw big audiences like the host teams in their home countries. There are a number of venues with a capacity of 40,000 seats or fewer, like Geodis Park in Nashville, Tenn., and San Diego's Snapdragon Stadium, that could make the cut in the end. Tournament organizers are entertaining the idea that strong atmospheres in smaller stadiums might be preferable to half-full venues for games that are not expected to welcome large audiences, though a final decision has yet to be made.
The vast majority of games are likely to be staged in the U.S., just as they were for the men's World Cup this year.Questions about the economic modelThere is little concern about North America's ability to host the Women's World Cup as far as the economics go. The U.S. alone is as ideal a market as any for a women's sporting event and has been for decades -- around 14 million people in the U.S. watched the national team beat China in the final via an iconic penalty shootout in 1999, while that tournament generated a $4 million profit on its $30 million operating costs. The question for 2031, though, is who will actually make money.The U.S. cities that hosted the men's World Cup this year spent the months before and after the tournament complaining about the economics, the local host committees footing bills that reportedly ran as high as $150 million per city to actually stage the tournament. The host committees at times successfully lobbied the Trump administration for federal funding, but they continued to express concerns about the division of costs between the cities and FIFA. The host committees were also reportedly waiting for a further $1 million weeks after the World Cup ended despite a pledge from FIFA president Gianni Infantino.
Potential host cities for the 2031 World Cup will likely advocate for a different split of the costs this time around, and the same could be true for the U.K.-set 2035 tournament. Local officials in the U.S. are reportedly contemplating banding together with the support of U.S. Soccer in the hopes of negotiating more favorable contracts with FIFA and avoiding fierce competition between the host cities that would strengthen FIFA's negotiating position.

title: The buyout economics of the 2026-27 coaching carousel - CBS Sports
description: The 2026-27 college football coaching carousel is in full swing, and these teams will have to pony up to pay off
body:
The 2026-27 college football coaching carousel is in full swing, and these teams will have to pony up to pay off their former coaches
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:51 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        TCU became the fourth Power Four program to fire its head coach on Sunday when it dismissed Sonny Dykes after five seasons. TCU joined Baylor, North Carolina State and Maryland as the coaching carousel finally got spinning in late October. With each firing comes a high financial cost to move on from the coach. What is each school paying to fire its coach, and where could it go next? CBS Sports breaks it down below.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Arkansas StateFired coach: Butch Jones (30-43 in 6 seasons)Cost: $1.5 million The former Tennessee coach's foray back into being a head coach had some highlights like an 8-5 season in 2024 but never quite panned out like Arkansas State hoped. Jones had spent years working for Nick Saban at Alabama when Arkansas State gave him another shot, and it seemed to make sense for both sides. Jones could rejuvenate his career and Arkansas State could return to the prominence it experienced with Gus Malzahn, Hugh Freeze and Bryan Harsin. The Jones era, though, got off to a rough start (5-19 in first two seasons) and other Sun Belt programs passed the Red Wolves. Jones did stabilize the situation and led Arkansas State to three straight bowl games, but it wasn't enough to save him when his program stumbled out to a 4-6 record in 2026. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    BaylorFired coach: Dave Aranda (40-40 in 7 seasons)Cost: Reportedly $12 millionBaylor fired Dave Aranda on Sunday following disappointing losses to TCU and Kansas. Aranda had seemingly cooled his seat with a 4-1 start, but those losses ultimately doomed him. As a private school, Baylor does not release coaching contracts the way public schools must. The buyout figure was believed to be approximately $12 million last season, while Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger reported that same figure for this year's cost. Candidates to replace Aranda include Boise State's Spencer Danielson and UTSA's Jeff Traylor. Check out the full list of Baylor coaching options here. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Florida StateFired coach: Mike Norvell Cost: Approximately $49 million (41-39 in 7 seasons)Florida State pulled the plug on Mike Norvell after another disappointing home loss, this one a 36-24 defeat to Clemson. The nearly $49 million Florida State will pay Norvell is the third-highest in college football history, behind only Texas A&M and Jimbo Fisher ($77 million) and LSU and Brian Kelly ($54 million). Norvell entered the season on the hottest seat in college football after back-to-back losing seasons in 2024 and 2025. The expectation was at least 7 or 8 wins in 2026 for Norvell to keep his job, but a 3-5 start led to his dismissal. 
Florida State had already fired athletic director Michael Alford earlier in the year, and will have a drastically new look to its athletic department moving forward. Early candidates to replace Norvell include Duke's Manny Diaz, Wake Forest's Jake Dickert and ACC Network analyst Jimbo Fisher. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    MarylandFired coach: Mike Locksley (39-54 in 8 seasons)Cost: $9.75 million Maryland kicked off the coaching carousel when it fired Mike Locksley on Wednesday. The school owes Locksley around $9.75 million with no offsets if he takes another job. Half of that $9.75 million is due to Locksley within sixty days. He had been under contract through 2028 but was let go after a 2-5 start to the season, which included losses to Rutgers, Virginia Tech and UCLA. 
Candidates to replace Locksley include Wake Forest's Jake Dickert, New Mexico's Jason Eck and Memphis' Charles Huff. Full candidates list here. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    North Carolina StateFired coach: Dave Doeren (98-73 in 14 seasons)Cost: $10.3 million NC State opted for a rare Saturday afternoon firing when it dumped Dave Doeren after 14 seasons. There had been rumblings before the season that this could be Doeren's last in Raleigh, but that was centered around a possible retirement and not a firing. Instead, NC State will pay approximately $10.3 million to buy out the remainder of a contract set to run through 2029. NC State owes Doeren a little more than $600,000 within the next 30 days, and can then pay the remainder in monthly installments. The 54-year-old Doeren does have a clause in his contract requiring him to make reasonable efforts to find another job, which could offset the buyout NC State owes. The early candidate to watch to replace Doeren is former NC State quarterback great Philip Rivers. More on Rivers and NC State here. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Sam Houston StateFired coach: Phil Longo (3-17 in 2 seasons)Cost: $1.6 millionPhil Longo did not make it through a second season following a 1-7 start. The former Wisconsin and North Carolina offensive coordinator could never get it going with his Air Raid-style offense. Longo went 1-11 in Conference USA play before being dismissed on Oct. 28th. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    TCUFired coach: Sonny Dykes (41-23 in 5 seasons)Cost: More than $20 millionSonny Dykes couldn't sustain the highs of a 2022 run to the national championship game in a tenure that ended on Nov. 22. After losing to Georgia in the title game, Dykes' TCU program slipped to 5-7 and missed a bowl game the next season. He rebounded with a pair of 9-4 seasons in 2024 and 2025, but his name seemed to linger on hot-seat discussions. Still, TCU gave him an extension in April that ran through 2030. The exact terms of Dykes' buyout aren't known because TCU is a private school, but multiple industry sources told CBS Sports the number is upwards of $20 million.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    UTEPFired coach: Scotty Walden (6-28 in 3 seasons)Cost: $1 millionScotty Walden, one of the youngest head coaches in the FBS, lost his job Nov. 16th after a 1-9 start to the season. In one of the hardest jobs in college football, Walden never managed more than three wins in a season.

title: Would JuJu Watkins skip the 2027 WNBA Draft? Pros and cons of USC superstar spending another year in school - CBS Sports
description: Late last week, JuJu Watkins went off for a season-high 36 points, 11 rebounds, four assists, six steals and a block to lead No. 4 USC t
body:
Late last week, JuJu Watkins went off for a season-high 36 points, 11 rebounds, four assists, six steals and a block to lead No. 4 USC to a 78-69 win over Baylor and reinforce her status as the clear choice for the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 WNBA Draft. That pick, thanks to last week's WNBA Draft Lottery, is held by the Toronto Tempo. Of course, if she decides to turn pro, that is. Watkins missed all of last season with a torn ACL and is eligible to return to school for the 2027-28 season. Publicly, Watkins has maintained that she has not made up her mind. "As far as the next thing, honestly, all my attention is here," Watkins told CBS Sports' Isabel Gonzalez following the win over Baylor. "I really can't say what I'm doing because I don't know. I'm just locked in on everything we have going on here, honestly."
If Watkins truly is undecided, she has until April to make up her mind. In the wake of the draft lottery and her most recent comment, let's take a look at the pros and cons of declaring for the 2027 WNBA Draft. 

        
            
                2027 WNBA Mock Draft: JuJu Watkins, Hannah Hidalgo go 1-2 to Tempo and Comets
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Pro: Watkins is going to be the No. 1 pickIf Watkins declares for the 2027 WNBA Draft, she is going to be the No. 1 overall pick. First and foremost, that is a tremendous honor, one that players dream about growing up. There are also numerous benefits to having certainty about where you'll begin your professional career months in advance. Off the court, Watkins (or, more likely, her team) could start handling all sorts of logistics. On the court, Watkins would know she's joining a Tempo team with a Hall of Fame coach in Sandy Brondello that is ready to be competitive right away. The Tempo were 9-9 last season with the No. 4 offense in the league before an array of injuries precipitated an all-time tanking effort. With Watkins in the mix, the Tempo could contend for a playoff spot in 2027, especially if they shore up their frontcourt in free agency. Watkins could lose all of that if she returns to school. The 2028 draft class includes Sarah Strong, who is arguably an even better prospect, and on top of that, it's impossible to predict what the 2028 lottery might look like. 
Con: No offseasonThe 2027 WNBA Draft is set for April 12, a week after the 2027 Final Four. Training camps would begin shortly after the draft, followed by WNBA opening night on May 8, according to ESPN. The 2027 WNBA regular season will see teams play a record 50 games and will go as late as Oct. 24. Watkins and USC opened play this season on Nov. 2, but had been practicing long before that. Barring an extremely early exit from the 2027 Women's NCAA Tournament, Watkins would not get an offseason and would wind up playing for essentially a full calendar year. That's the case for every draft pick, but is particularly notable for Watkins given her recent injury. Sitting out 18 months to rehab a torn ACL, then immediately playing 12 months in a row would not be ideal. If she returned to school, she would get a full offseason to give her knee a break. 
Pro: Get to start professional careerBack in December of 2024, months before she tore her ACL, Watkins made an appearance on Sarah Spain's podcast and argued for the WNBA to change its eligibility rules. Currently, domestic draft entrants must be at least 22 years old in the calendar year in which the draft takes place to be eligible. International prospects, on the other hand, only need to be 20 years old. "I definitely think we should have the option [to leave school early]," Watkins said. "There's just been such a growth in college basketball where it's like, why would you want to leave? Because you're able to have that experience and build your brand here in college as well. I would definitely say we should have the option, but I think college is a way to prepare us for the pros as well. So, I don't know. It's a touchy subject, but I'm for it."Watkins' injury significantly changed her circumstances, but even so, it would be somewhat surprising to see her return to school for a fifth year after arguing that players should be able to leave school early. And while college basketball is a great platform, players ultimately want to prove themselves on the professional level. Declaring for the 2027 draft would allow Watkins to do so as soon as possible. 
Con: One less chance at a national championshipWatkins led USC to the Elite Eight as a freshman, was injured in the second round as a sophomore and missed the tournament as a junior. If she declares for the draft after this season, this will be her last chance to compete for a national championship. "To come here, have my family here, have an even bigger family now that I'm here in the staff, the coaches, my teammates, it's a dream come true and I couldn't have wished for anything better," Watkins, a Los Angeles native, said early in her freshman season. She added that she wanted to "definitely have to have a natty" by her senior year. The fourth-ranked Trojans are one of the favorites this season, and may well win their first title since 1984. If they do, you would have to imagine that would make it even easier for Watkins to leave. But if they don't, how much would leaving college without a title weigh on Watkins? 
Pro: Get to be a star in another countryAfter the Tempo won the lottery, there was a lot of speculation about Watkins staying in school so she wouldn't have to play in Canada. Certainly, going to live in another country has to be a consideration, and it's possible she stays in school because she wants to play for an American team. But, at least from an outside perspective, there are more positives than negatives about playing for the Tempo. Starting with the aforementioned fact that they're ready to be competitive. Plus, summer in Toronto is about as nice as you can get in terms of weather. Finally, you would have an entire country to yourself. The Tempo are truly Canada's team, as we saw in July when 20,996 fans filled the Bell Centre in Montreal for the Tempo's matchup with the Dallas Wings, which set the league's single-game attendance record. 
"From Day 1, we've believed this team could unite fans across the country, and tonight they showed the world what's possible," Tempo president Teresa Resch said after the game. "This moment belongs to every fan who filled the Bell Centre, every player who inspired the next generation, and everyone who believed Canada was ready for this. We're incredibly proud, deeply grateful, and even more excited about what's ahead." The Tempo played multiple games in Montreal last season, as well as two games in Vancouver. If Watkins declares for the draft, she could become an icon for an entire country, rather than a single city in the U.S. Con: Short-term moneyUCLA coach Cori Close said last week that despite the historic new WNBA collective bargaining agreement, some players in college still make more than A'ja Wilson -- $1.4 million in 2026 -- and all six of the Bruins players who were selected in the 2026 WNBA Draft took a pay cut as rookies. While it's unclear exactly how much Watkins is getting directly from USC, we can safely assume it's at least seven figures considering she's a bigger star than anyone on UCLA last season. 
Again, assuming that is the case, Watkins would take a pay cut in 2027 if she declares for the draft. And that's before considering what USC might offer her to stick around for a fifth year. Due to the WNBA's new revenue-sharing model, the 2027 salary cap has not been set, so we don't have the official rookie scale contracts yet. But the maximum Watkins could make as the No. 1 overall pick in 2027 is $565,000. At that figure, her four-year rookie contract would be worth $2.5 million, per Her Hoops Stats, not including a potential EPIC extension. USC might be able to pay Watkins more than her entire rookie contract to stay for a fifth year. Regardless, it's clear that Watkins would make more short-term money by staying at USC. 
Pro: Better chance at the OlympicsLos Angeles will host the 2028 Olympics, and Watkins has made it clear that she wants to suit up for Team USA in her hometown. "That's been my North Star this whole time, so to get this opportunity means a lot," Watkins said last year when she was invited to a USA Basketball training camp. It's clear that USA Basketball sees Watkins as a key piece moving forward, but no rookie has made the Olympic team since Breanna Stewart in 2016, and there have been multiple high-profile rookie snubs from the national team in the last two major tournaments: Caitlin Clark in the 2024 Olympics and Olivia Miles in the 2026 World Cup. Watkins is bigger, more physical and a much better defender than Clark or Miles, and the Americans lack wing depth, all of which gives Watkins a realistic chance to make the 2028 Olympic team even if she stays in school and doesn't turn pro until 2028. However, there's no question that declaring for the 2027 draft and having a full year of WNBA experience under her belt would improve her chances of making the final roster for Los Angeles.

description: Here's everything you need to know about the NFL for Nov. 23
body:
Here's everything you need to know about the NFL for Nov. 23
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:29 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            19 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Hello football friends, and welcome to the Monday edition of the Pick Six newsletter!It is officially Thanksgiving week, and if you're an NFL fan, that means you should probably just go ahead and clear your schedule from now until the end of the month because there is going to be an NFL game on almost every day. You get one game tonight (Bengals at Commanders)You get one game on Wednesday (Packers at Rams)You get three on Thursday (Bears at Lions, Eagles at Cowboys, Chiefs at Bills)You get one on Friday (Broncos at Steelers)You get a normal schedule of 10 games on SundayAnd you get another game next Monday (Panthers at Buccaneers)That means there will be at least one game in six of the next eight days. Is that more football than I need? Probably, but I always eat more turkey than I need on Thanksgiving and never regret it, so I don't think I'll regret it if I watch every game between now and Nov. 30. You also won't regret reading today's newsletter, so let's get to the rundown. As always, here's your daily reminder to tell all your friends to sign up for the newsletter. To get them signed up, just click here.  
1. NFL Week 11 grades: 49ers ace Mexico City test
                                                                    Manuel Velasquez/Getty Images
                                                            Welcome to my favorite part of the Monday newsletter: The part where I hand out grades for every team that played. The easiest grade to hand out this week went to the 49ers, who destroyed the Vikings in an NFC Showdown. The 49ers spent the entire week practicing in Colorado to get prepared for the 7,350-foot elevation in Mexico City, and it definitely showed. With that in mind, let's get to a few of the grades from Week 11: 49ers 35-10 over VikingsVikings takeaway: If this game proved one thing, it's that the Vikings simply aren't in the same weight class as the 49ers right now. Brian Flores' vaunted defense had no answers for Kyle Shanahan's offense. If this were a boxing match, it would be a TKO. The Vikings' defense almost seemed shocked at how easily the 49ers moved the ball against Flores' blitz-happy offense. Of course, the bigger concern for Minnesota might be the offense. Adding Kirk Cousins was supposed to improve things, but he got rattled early and never looked comfortable. After starting the season 6-0, the Vikings are now in a tailspin: At 7-3, there's now a very real chance that this team ends up missing the postseason. GRADE: D-49ers takeaway: This was a total annihilation by a 49ers team that outclassed the Vikings in every way possible. The Vikings defense has been blitzing everyone into submission all season, but they found out you can't do that to Brock Purdy. The 49ers QB burned the Vikings almost anytime they tried to blitz, finishing the night 16-for-18 for 195 yards and two touchdowns when blitzed, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Purdy's 148.8 passer rating against the Vikings he Vikings had no answers for San Francisco's offense. The addition of Mike Evans continues to look like one of the best signings of the offseason: The 6-foot-5 receiver gave Purdy a large target and the QB took advantage of that by throwing him six paasses that went for 109 yards. This entire game was a masterclass by Kyle Shanahan. The biggest surprise of this win might have been how well the 49ers' defense played. That side of the ball delivered the unofficial knockout blow with Ji'Ayir Brown's pick-six that put the 49ers up 28-10 just before halftime. The 49ers made a statement in this game and that statement is that they might be the best team in the NFC, if not the entire NFL. GRADE: A+Panthers 35-33 over RavensRavens takeaway: For the fourth straight game, the Ravens turned the ball over multiple times, and for the fourth straight game, the Ravens lost. This team has been plagued by bad mistakes in recent weeks, and that was once again the case here: Justice Hill fumbled the ball out of the end zone for a Panthers' touchback, Derrick Henry fumbled away a short pass in the fourth quarter, and LaJohntay Wester muffed two punts (losing one of them). Then Jacoby Brissett threw the game away with an interception on Baltimore's final offensive drive. It was a comedy of errors, but there's nothing funny about the Ravens' season, which is spiraling out of control.. GRADE: CPanthers takeaway: The Panthers showed some serious resiliency in this game: Their offense took a safety, their special teams gave up a return touchdown and the defense surrendered over 400 yards, but Carolina still pulled out the win. The Panthers won because they made big plays in clutch moments, and sometimes that's all you need to win games in the NFL. The opportunistic defense forced two huge fumbles, including a brilliant peanut punch by Will Lee that saved a TD in the first half. Tyrel Dodson also made a massive play, sealing the win with an interception of Jacoby Brissett in the fourth quarter. Offensively, the Panthers got off to a slow start, but Chuba Hubbard and Bryce Young eventually found a groove. Hubbard outplayed Derrick Henry while bulldozing his way through Baltimore's defense for 120 yards and two touchdowns. Young engineered a game-winning drive, going 4 of 4 for 37 yards to set up Ryan Fitzgerald's go-ahead field goal in the fourth quarter. Everyone came up clutch for the Panthers, and heading into Thanksgiving, this feels like the best team in the NFC South. GRADE: C+Giants 23-18 over JaguarsJaguars takeaway: The Giants might have just given other teams a recipe to beat the Jaguars: Punch them in the mouth and see what happens. The Jags offensive line was no match for the Giants' pass-rush, and that created a lot of problems for Jacksonville's offense. Trevor Lawrence couldn't get into any sort of rhythm, and he ended up throwing two UGLY interceptions on a day when he was also sacked three times. With Lawrence flustered, the Jags struggled in key situations, especially in the fourth quarter, when they were 0-for-9 on third-down attempts (Lawrence also threw an incompletion on a failed fourth-and-1 in the third quarter). The Jags were starting to look invincible after winning three straight games and averaging 38.3 points, but this loss was a reality check. GRADE: CGiants takeaway: There's a reason the Giants are leading the NFC East: their defense. Abdul Carter, who tallied two of New York's three sacks, led a pass rush that kept Trevor Lawrence on the run for nearly all four quarters. The defense won this game in the red zone: The Jags made six trips inside New York's 20-yard line but came away with only one TD. Offensively, the Giants almost choked this game away in the second half, but J.J. McCarthy threw a big pass late in the fourth quarter that helped New York run out the clock. If the Giants offense starts playing at the same level as the defense, this team can beat anyone. GRADE: A-As for the other grades that we've handed out so far in Week 11, you can check those out here. 2. NFL Week 11 winners and losers: Steelers have a day in PhiladelphiaYou can't have a week of NFL action without winners and losers, so here are some of them. Carter Bahns put together this week's list of winners and losers, and we'll check out his losers below. It was such an ugly week for the Steelers that he actually put them down twice on this list. 
LOSERS Steelers. The last time the Steelers beat the Philadelphia Eagles in the City of Brotherly Love? 1965. Granted, as members of opposite conferences, the in-state rivals only play every few years. But this is a losing streak that now spans 12 games after Sunday's 19-16 result, which went in favor of the Eagles.  This was the kind of matchup that was supposed to help the Steelers bounce back from last week's no-show against the Cincinnati Bengals and work their way back toward the top of the AFC North. Instead, they lost to a team that hadn't won a game since September and started Joe Milton at quarterback. It is far too early to call it a devastating loss, but if the Steelers finish the season a game short of a playoff berth, it is a contest they will look back on as one they should have gotten.DK Metcalf. As if the loss to the Eagles was not bad enough for DK Metcalf and the Steelers, the wide receiver made his day even worse with an inexcusable decision. Metcalf had been jawing at Philadelphia defenders all game and took it to another level when he poked Cooper DeJean in the eye a little more than halfway through the third quarter. That exchange drew an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty  (Metcalf's second of the game) and prompted his ejection from the game.Trevor Lawrence. High yardage total aside, Trevor Lawrence had a day to forget. His 301 passing yards were more a product of the large passing volume required of him in a loss than anything else. The New York Giants defense had him pressing in a 23-18 loss and forced him into a number of errors including two interceptions, a pick on a 2-point attempt, three sacks and a whopping 22 incompletions. It took until the fourth quarter for Lawrence to lead the Jaguars to a touchdown, but by that point, it was too late. If you want to see Carter's list of winners (and a couple of other losers), be sure to click here. 3. Overreactions from Week 11: Will Ravens fire Jesse Minter?
                                                                    Todd Olszewski/Getty Images
                                                            Everyone on the internet loves to overreact, and that's especially true when we're talking about the NFL. Zach Pereles looked at several things that happened during Week 11, so decide for yourself whether we're all overreacting.  Statement: Jesse Minter will be one-and-done in Baltimore.Overreaction or reality: Overreaction. Lots of the Ravens' issues are out of first-year coach Jesse Minter's control. The Lamar Jackson injuries, obviously, threw the season way off course. Even Sunday's game was another example of the things Minter can't control going wrong. Justice Hill fumbled 1 yard from the end zone. LaJohntay Wester muffed two punts, one of which the Panthers recovered. Derrick Henry also lost a fumble. It's been a season from hell.  But there are plenty of issues Minter has been responsible for — or at least hasn't fixed — this year. Regarded as a defensive whiz after two years as the Chargers' defensive coordinator, he now oversees a defense that ranks in the bottom half of the league in yards per game and yards per play, and in the bottom 10 in yards per pass attempt and takeaways. Simply put, it's been underwhelming at best for a team expected to contend for a championship. But the Ravens won't fire Minter at season's end. There are big-picture questions about Jackson and the entire roster, but Minter should get an offseason to tweak and improve his defense and fit it better to his defenders. 
Statement: The Buccaneers have a serious Baker Mayfield problem.Overreaction or reality: Reality. The Buccaneers extended Mayfield with a three-year, $165 million deal just before the season began, after it seemed like an extension wouldn't happen.  Tampa Bay must be wishing it hadn't made the deal. Mayfield is constantly banged up - he's dealing with plantar fasciitis in addition to the thumb injury that caused him to miss several games already this year - and he can't physically make his play style work. How the Buccaneers overcome this is TBD, because there are no realistic easy answers. Statement: Jahmyr Gibbs will win Offensive Player of the Year.  Overreaction or reality: Reality. It wasn't always pretty, but Jahmyr Gibbs ground out 118 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns in the Lions' 31-21 win over the Buccaneers. He's up to 1,502 yards from scrimmage this season and on pace to finish with 2,553. That would break Chris Johnson's all-time record of 2,509 from 2009.  That, one would think, would clinch an Offensive Player of the Year award for Gibbs. Even if he doesn't break the record, Gibbs would be a deserving winner, so long as he keeps producing. He's had at least 110 yards from scrimmage in all but two games.There are plenty more overreactions, and you can check them out here.4. 12 crazy stats from Week 11: Titans might have the worst defense ever Every Sunday night, I get an email from our research department here at CBS Sports, and it always includes some crazy stats about the games that were just played. 
With that in mind, here are 10 crazy stats from Week 12: Titans defense hits rock bottom. Following their 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday, the Titans have now surrendered at least 40 points and 450 yards in three straight games. That's the first time in the Super Bowl era that we've ever seen that happen. The last defense to give up those numbers in three straight games came all the way back in 1964 when the Broncos did it. Cam Ward on the cusp of history he probably wants no part of. With the Titans losing on Sunday, Cam Ward has now lost 23 games in his career, which is tied for the most in NFL history for a QB in his first two seasons. If Wards loses just one more game this season, he'll have the most losses ever through two years. The good news for Ward is that both quarterbacks who hit the 23-loss mark before him — Warren Moon and Steve DeBerg — both had long careers, and Moon ended up being voted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Jahmyr joins exclusive club. With 118 total yards and two touchdowns, Jahmyr Gibbs now has 1,502 total yards and 15 touchdowns on the season. That makes him just the fourth player in NFL history and first player since 1995 (Emmitt Smith) to record at least 1,500 yards and 15 touchdowns in his team's first 10 games. Dynamic duo. Not only did Gibbs scored a touchdown on Sunday, but so did Amon-Ra St. Brown. This marks the 25th time that both players have scored a TD in the same game, which is the fifth-most for any set of teammates in NFL history, trailing only Emmitt Smith/Michael Irvin (32), Lenny Moore/Raymond Berry (31), LaDainian Tomlinson/Antonio Gates (28) and Jerry Rice/John Taylor (28). It seems like it's only a matter of time before Gibbs and St. Brown break the record. Bears don't have to play from behind. The Bears didn't trail for a single second against the Saints on Sunday. They've now gone five straight games without trailing. That's the team's longest streak since 1959. The Bears haven't trailed since their 31-7 loss to the Packers in Week 5. Bills a lock for the AFC title game? With their win over the Dolphins, the Bills are now 9-1. This is the fourth time in the Super Bowl era that they've started at least 9-1, and on the previous three occasions (1988, 1990, 1991), they made it to the AFC title game all three times. Two of those ended with a trip to the Super Bowl. Old Man Kelce has a big game. Travis Kelce scored two touchdowns against the Cardinals, which is the only notable thing to come out of that one-sided drubbing. The outing makes Kelce the fourth-oldest player in NFL history to score two touchdowns in a game. At 37 years and 48 days, Kelce only trails Jerry Rice (40 years, 29 days), Charlie Joiner (37 years, 336 days) and Tony Gonzalez (37 years, 214 days). Old man, Rodgers, pulls off rarity. The Steelers didn't win on Sunday, but Aaron Rodgers did lead the team in rushing. At 42 years and 355 days, that makes Rodgers the second-oldest player in NFL history to lead his team in rushing yards, trailing only Tom Brady, who was 44 years, 54 days when he led the Buccaneers in rushing for a game in 2021. Steelers not feeling the brotherly love. With their loss on Sunday, the Steelers have now gone 61 years without winning a game in Philadelphia. In that span, the Steelers have lost 12 straight games in Philly. Their last victory in the City of Brotherly Love came all the way back in 1965. Home sweet home. Home teams have gone 10-1 in Week 11 and if the Commanders can pull off an upset on Monday night, that would improve the mark to 11-1, which would be the best single-week combined home record for NFL teams since Week 7 in 1998. Kirk Cousins meltdown in Mexico. The Vikings QB threw a pick-six against the 49ers on Sunday night, which marks the second time that he's thrown a pick-six against them. The first one came two weeks ago while Cousins was playing for the Raiders, which makes Cousins the first player in NFL history to throw a pick-six against the same opponent with two different teams. Vikings try 71-yard field goal after fair-catch kick. For the first time in two years, we got a field goal attempt after a fair-catch kick. Just before halftime on Sunday night, the Vikings took advantage of an obscure rule that allows you to attempt a field goal after making a fair catch. The Vikings tried an absolutely massive 71-yarder and almost made it, but Will Reichard's kick ended up falling about a yard short. You can read more about the crazy play here. Cowboys get another scorigami. For the second straight week, the Cowboys were involved in a scorigami. Their 51-30 win over the Titans marks the first time in NFL history that a game has ever ended with that final score. The Cowboys also had a new final score in Week 10 when they lost to the 49ers 46-40. The Cowboys are the first time since 2016 to record a scorigami in back-to-back weeks. If you see any other fun facts, feel free to tweet them at me.5. Monday night preview: Picks and best bets for Bengals at Commanders
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            If you like offensive fireworks, then you're definitely going to want to make sure to park yourself in front of a TV for tonight's game. The Bengals (7-2) and one of the hottest offenses in the NFL will be traveling to Washington to take on a desperate Commanders (3-5-1) team.With the the Giants and Cowboys both winning on Sunday, the Commanders need a win to keep pace in the NFC East. If they lose, that will put a huge dent in their division title hopes. As for the Bengals, they're on a five-game winning streak and they have a chance to take full control of the AFC North following the Steelers' loss on Sunday. With that in mind, here's one reason why each team should be feeling confident going into the game: 
Why the Bengals can win: Heading into Week 11, the Commanders have surrendered the second-most passing yards per game this year, so there's a good chance that Joe Burrow could carve them up. Burrow has already faced the worst passing defense (Tennessee), and he threw for 462 yards and three touchdowns in that game. He faced the third-worst passing defense (Pittsburgh) and he threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are both playing at a high level and if you combine that with the fact that Burrow is on a hot streak, the Bengals could put up some big offensive numbers tonight. Why the Commanders can win: The Bengals have looked unbeatable over the past few weeks, but if there's one key to beating them, it's in the ability to run the ball well. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt making his return tonight, the Commanders will be in a good spot and if they can get their rushing attack going, that will burn up the clock and keep Joe Burrow off the field. The Commanders came close to beating the Rams (20-13) and they came close to beating the 49ers (23-17), so they've proven they can play with the top teams in the NFL, now, it's just a matter of actually pulling off the upset. You can get a full preview of the game from Jared Dubin by clicking here.If you're thinking about betting on the game, here are a couple of props. ONE PASSING PROP I LIKE: Joe Burrow OVER 2.5 passing touchdowns (-129 at DraftKings): Burrow has gone over 2.5 touchdown passes in five straight games. Gonzalez was at the helm for both Saturday's defeat to the Kansas City Current and the 2025 loss in the NWSL Championship to Gotham FC

        The Washington Spirit parted ways with head coach Adrian Gonzalez on Monday, less than 48 hours after a 2-1 loss to the Kansas City Current that marked the team's third successive defeat in the NWSL Championship.Gonzalez was an assistant on the 2024 team that lost to the Orlando Pride in the final but succeeded Jonatan Giraldez after he left for France's OL Lyonnes midway through the 2025 campaign. He was a finalist for the NWSL's coach of the year award last season and maintained a consistency that has been a trademark for the Spirit in recent years, ensuring they continued to be serial contenders for titles under both Giraldez and Gonzalez.For all their ambition, though, the Spirit have struggled to win major titles in the years since businesswoman Michele Kang took over the club in 2022. Their only title since is the 2025 Challenge Cup, a one-off game against the Pride, and have failed to win the NWSL Shield despite inching close on a handful of occasions while also falling short in the NWSL Championship games. They also failed to win the Concacaf W Champions Cup earlier this year, losing 5-3 to Club America in the final."I'm incredibly proud of what we've accomplished together at the Washington Spirit and grateful to the players, staff, ownership and supporters for their commitment and support throughout my time here," Gonzalez said in a club statement. "It has been an honor to lead this group, and I'm especially proud of the resilience and character the team has shown. A special thank you to the Spirit fans, who make this club truly unique. The connection and bond we've built with you has meant so much to me and made my time here even more special. Your passion and support are something I will always remember. While this chapter comes to an end, I'm excited for what lies ahead for the club and wish everyone continued success."
Gonzalez's departure also comes after Haley Carter became the president of soccer operations in the build-up to the 2026 season. Carter was previously with the Orlando Pride, who won both the NWSL Shield and NWSL Championship in 2024 after years of being a bottom-dweller in the league."We are grateful to Adrian for his leadership and the success he has helped bring to the Spirit over the past three seasons," Carter said in a statement. "He has led the team with class and professionalism and made a lasting contribution to this club. As we plan for the Spirit's future, all parties believe a change in leadership is necessary to build on that success and achieve our long-term sporting goals."
The search for Gonzalez's successor is underway and is likely to center around the Spirit's continuing quest to win the NWSL's top titles.
